gloss: A cookery book; the title means 'Varieties of Delicacies'.
A long coat fastened across the chest.
A gold coin.
Bamboo manna, a medicine made from a deposit found in bamboo.
The ceremony at which a child begins to read, starting with the words 'In the name of God'.
A box with four compartments for spices served to guests.
A board game played with dice.
A weight, one sixteenth of a ser (about two ounces).
The chief minister of a princely state.
A covered litter in which women were carried.
A long scarf worn over the head and shoulders.
The gift of money given at Eid.
The opening chapter of the Qur'an, recited over food offered in someone's memory or for a blessing.
A pudding of ground rice and milk.
A card game played with round painted cards.
A betel leaf folded with areca nut and spices.
One who knows the Qur'an by heart.
The pilgrimage to Mecca.
A woman who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca; in this book, the trickster who cheats Akbari.
A physician of the Greek-Arabic (unani) school.
The meal that breaks the day's fast in Ramzan.
Sweets fried in a deep pan.
A simple dish of rice and lentils cooked together.
A measure of distance; in this book, two miles.
An elementary school.
A maidservant, usually an older woman who cooks.
'As God has willed': said in praise, to ward off the evil eye.
A man learned in religion; also a title of respect.
The henna ceremony before a wedding.
Sweet rice cooked with meat.
Betel leaf, chewed with areca nut and lime.
Rice cooked with meat and spices.
The seclusion of women from men outside the family.
A rich meat curry.
Thickened sweetened milk.
A weight of about two pounds.
One of the thirty parts into which the Qur'an is divided for reading.
The revenue officer in charge of a sub-district.
A woman teacher.
The alms every Muslim with means must give each year, a fortieth of his wealth.
Sweet rice coloured with saffron; also scented tobacco.
